note: The exact prompts every r10 entrant received: one system and one user message per run. Official rounds used them unchanged.

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a sea container and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the container.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. along the length: between 35% and 65% of the length.
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form at most two blocks: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a sea container and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the container.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. along the length: between 35% and 65% of the length.
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form at most two blocks: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a truck and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the cargo space.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. the total weight (cargo + tare) splits between kingpin and bogie like a beam on two supports at kingpin_from_front_mm and bogie_from_front_mm; neither may exceed its max (not checked when the total is within both limits).
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form one block: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a truck and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the cargo space.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. the total weight (cargo + tare) splits between kingpin and bogie like a beam on two supports at kingpin_from_front_mm and bogie_from_front_mm; neither may exceed its max (not checked when the total is within both limits).
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form one block: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a truck and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the cargo space.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. the total weight (cargo + tare) splits between kingpin and bogie like a beam on two supports at kingpin_from_front_mm and bogie_from_front_mm; neither may exceed its max (not checked when the total is within both limits).
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form one block: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a truck and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the cargo space.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. the total weight (cargo + tare) splits between kingpin and bogie like a beam on two supports at kingpin_from_front_mm and bogie_from_front_mm; neither may exceed its max (not checked when the total is within both limits).
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form one block: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a truck and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the cargo space.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. the total weight (cargo + tare) splits between kingpin and bogie like a beam on two supports at kingpin_from_front_mm and bogie_from_front_mm; neither may exceed its max (not checked when the total is within both limits).
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form one block: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a sea container and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the container.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. along the length: between 35% and 65% of the length.
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form at most two blocks: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given a sea container and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the container.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.

x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. along the length: between 35% and 65% of the length.
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form at most two blocks: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

runs.system:
You are an expert load planner. You will be given an air container (ULD) and a cargo manifest. Produce a complete, physically legal loading plan.

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is the front-left floor corner of the container.
x runs along the length from the front wall (x = 0) to the doors (x = interior length).
y runs across the width from the left wall. z runs up from the floor.
All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

Hard rules (a layout that breaks any of them is illegal):
1. Every placed item lies fully inside the cargo space: x >= 0, y >= 0, z >= 0, x + dx <= length, y + dy <= width, z + dz <= height.
   Sloped sides: a sloped side {side, overhang_mm, height_mm} rises from the edge of the flat floor, overhang_mm in from that wall, to height_mm up at the wall ("y+" is the wall at y = width, "y-" the wall at y = 0). An item whose bottom is at z may come no closer to that wall than overhang_mm x (1 - z / height_mm); above height_mm the full width is free.
2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.
4. If tiltable is false the item stays upright: dz must equal its height_mm (it may only turn about the vertical axis).
5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
   Exception for sloped sides: an item may instead lean on the slope with its outer bottom edge, nothing under it, at z equal to the slope's height under that edge (height_mm x reach / overhang_mm, where reach is how far the item extends past the edge of the flat floor; within 1.5 mm), provided that z is at most 15% of dy and at least 60% of dy, and the item's centre, lie over the flat floor.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.
9. Balance. Skipped for a light load: total manifest weight below 15% of max_payload_kg, total manifest volume below 25% of the cargo space, and no item of 500 kg or more (all three). Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the floor) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the width from the left wall;
   b. along the length: between 35% and 65% of the length.
10. Slender piles: an item standing on another item's top, together with the comparable items directly below it, may be at most 5 times as tall as its narrowest braced width. An item's braced width is the narrower side of the block it stands in: the items at the same z that touch it side to side (gap at most 10 mm), each at least half as tall as its neighbour, chained; walls do not count, and a lone item's braced width is its own narrower side. The pile's narrowest braced width is the smallest over its items. The pile ends at the floor or at an item whose narrower side is more than 1.5 times the top item's narrower side; a pile that reaches the floor, and a single item on such a wider base, are not limited.

Loading practice, on the items standing on the floor (reported as a separate verdict, not part of legality):
- They form at most two blocks: a gap longer than 300 mm along x between them starts a new block.
- Items at least 85% of the width wide that share a footprint line up at the same y.

Also reported, never scored: floor load per item against max_floor_load_kg_m2, how far the floor block stands from the nearest end wall (more than 150 mm), more than 3 gaps over 60 mm across the width in one cross-section, items that could tip over in transport.

Place as many items as you legally can. Any item you cannot place goes in "unplaced".

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else after it, in this exact shape:
{"placements":[{"id":"I01","x":0,"y":0,"z":0,"dx":1200,"dy":800,"dz":1000}],"unplaced":["I07"]}

Coordinates are millimetres. The origin is one corner of the pallet deck, on its top surface.

All contact and overlap tests allow 1 mm of tolerance.

2. No two items overlap in 3D.
3. dx, dy, dz are the item's extents along x, y, z after you orient it, and must be a permutation of its length, width and height. Each item id appears at most once.

5. Support: an item with z > 0 must rest with at least 95% of its base area on the tops of items whose top is exactly at its z.
6. Nothing may rest on an item with stackable = false, nor on a fragile item that has no max_stack_kg above 0.
7. If an item has max_stack_kg, the total weight of everything at or above its top that overlaps its footprint (at any height) must not exceed it.
8. Total weight of placed items must not exceed max_payload_kg.

Otherwise the centre of gravity of placed cargo plus tare_kg (tare acts at the middle of the deck) must satisfy:
   a. across the width: between 40% and 60% of the deck width;
